//: This repository's own configuration. It is also the worked example the documentation refers to: an artifact whose delivery boundary is not a deployment.

verification.//stage1: Everything that can be proven without leaving the working tree.
verification.//stage2: The boundary here is the plugin loader, the installer, and — since #49 — a real agent session. Whether the gopnik-setup skill's conversation actually happens is a property of an agent, and an agent CLI on this machine is how you find out. Three verdicts called that unreachable while `claude` was installed. Since #73 the same applies to the gate itself: two fixtures one line of product code apart, which must come back with opposite verdicts.

verification.notes: Use the two isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR trees recorded under .git: installing into the real one changes the operator's own session. Each tree links only the active profile's credential file, proves that Claude sees the existing login, and keeps plugin state isolated; the temporary links disappear with the validated root. The clone must match the exact local HEAD, so an unpushed fix fails before conversation testing. The installer command preserves a pre-existing project-owned sentinel and proves all three skills exist. The English conversation starts from the README launcher and selects the agent-wide scope; the Russian conversation starts from the same launcher and selects repository-local scope. Both continue through the separate stand and access turns. Every turn resumes an explicit session from its fixture directory. The checked stream orders a successful Stage 1 helper result before a completed independent gopnik-critic agent and the final question, while the project check leaves an exact marker. The bounded oracle rejects internal defect reports, mixed-language Russian onboarding, and overlong or unsafe questions. The successful path removes its validated temporary root. Live Stage 2 still requires the operator's explicit authentication go-ahead. Since #76 a second setup conversation runs against the `stage1-gap` fixture, whose documented command covers only part of what the tree can execute: the run has to ask about the browser suite before recording anything, and the cell asserts both that the recorded Stage 1 ends up holding both commands and that the suite actually left its marker. That conversation is English only; the Russian cells stay on `hybrid`, where they also serve as the control that the new question is not asked on a project whose route already runs everything. #76 adds a second gate pair, `gate-ui-covered` and `gate-ui-gap`, one directory apart: the same UI change on a project whose stand is unreachable, with and without a loopback browser suite. Both have a green Stage 1 check, so the pair cannot be passed by reading exit codes — the covered side must show the suite ran, and the bare side must refuse a change to an interface nobody looked at.
